paras: The lynching of John Smith was the shooting of a Black man by a mob in Laurens County, Georgia, reported in late July 1881. Accused of attempting the outrage of Mrs. R. T. Downing, Smith was found asleep by a pursuing mob the next day and shot to death. The episode is known only from one short paragraph printed in two Ohio newspapers under the headline "An Easy Death."

The paragraph described Smith as "a notoriously bad negro and ex-Penitentiary convict" living in Laurens County. According to it, he entered the Downing home at night while the husband was away and attempted an outrage on Mrs. Downing. When she "screamed frantically," he fled without accomplishing his purpose, carrying his shoes and clothing in his hand.

The next day a mob gathered and set out in pursuit of Smith. The mob came upon him "while he was in a heavy sleep" and, without waking him, "riddled" his body with bullets. The paragraph gave no date, no exact place, no size for the mob and no names of those who fired.
No report of an inquest, arrest or prosecution appears in the coverage.

The Somerset Press and the Eaton Democrat, both Ohio papers, printed the identical paragraph on page 1 on July 28, 1881, without a dateline or credited source. Its headline, "An Easy Death," and its description of Smith as "notoriously bad" and a former convict presented the killing as a fitting end, and it stated the accusation as fact.
